name: VerusBridge supplemental-export parser divergence
summary: VerusProof did not reject a cross-chain-export output carrying the supplemental flag. A crafted output that Verus treated as inactive supplemental data was therefore parsed on Ethereum as an active export whose attacker-chosen transfer hash authorized unbacked ETH, tBTC, and USDC payouts.
notes: The Delegator's contracts[2] slot changed to VerusProof 0x5e8060ecbf415aa25f12c1d67fde832bd87dcfa1. Exhaustive pre-exploit upgrade-call review found no later write to this module slot.

The exploit transaction itself transferred exactly 1,625.36688649 native ETH, 103.56766017 tBTC, and 147,658.836798 USDC from the bridge to the attacker-controlled receiver. The USD total values ETH and tBTC at the nearest pre-anchor DefiLlama prices and USDC at par. Subsequent recovery is separate from this exploit-time gross-loss measurement.

The target is the defect-executing VerusProof module, so the age begins with its contracts[2] installation in March 2024. The February 2026 router update changed other modules and does not reset this code age.
